svg.text: Carrier board on a 14 x 20 hole perfboard for the 38-pin ESP32 DevKitC (Ellie)
Top view (component side) of an uncut 4 x 6 cm perfboard with 14 x 20 holes. Antenna end up, USB at the bottom.
The small parts sit UNDER the ESP32, between its two socket strips. Wires are soldered on the underside.

Row 1 and column 14 stay empty. The dashed rings are the four M2 screws
that hold the board on its posts in the box.
Narrow clone (pin rows 22.9 mm apart)? Its second row lands in column 12:
move D1, R3 and the orange run one column to the left.
How to read it
solid line: bare wire or solder bridge along the holes, underside
dashed curve: insulated wire, underside, joined only at its ends
black dot: a component leg or wire end goes in this hole
The board
• A 4 x 6 cm perfboard with 14 x 20 holes, used as bought. No cutting.
• Count the rows from the antenna end. The ESP32 pins use rows 2 to 20,
so its USB-end pin (5V) is in the last row and row 1 stays empty.
Parts on the board
Sockets
two 19-way strips: column 3 and column 13, rows 2 to 20
col 4 row 10 to col 7 row 10
R2 1 kΩ
col 4 row 11 to col 7 row 11
col 9 row 20 to col 12 row 20
Q1 NPN
legs in col 9: C row 10, B row 11, E row 12
2N2222 / PN2222 / 2N3904 / S8050: flat face towards column 13
BC337 / BC547: flat face towards column 3
col 9 row 9 to col 12 row 9, stripe at col 12
C1 220 µF
+ leg col 4 row 20, – leg (stripe) col 4 row 19, bent over to lie flat
towards column 9. No wider than 6.3 mm
MOTOR
red col 1 row 7, black col 1 row 8
PAW
col 1 row 12 and col 1 row 13 (either way round)
LED
short leg col 1 row 16, long leg col 1 row 17
Three insulated wires underneath
LED +: col 7 row 10 to col 1 row 17
motor +: col 12 row 9 to col 1 row 7
motor -: col 9 row 9 to col 1 row 8
Build tips
• Everything under the ESP32 must stay below 10 mm. Push Q1 down to the board.
• Solder the low parts and all the wiring first, then the two socket strips,
with the ESP32 plugged into them so it sets their spacing. Connectors last.
• Keep the red 5 V run on row 20 clear of the black run in column 4.
• Check with a meter before plugging the ESP32 in: no beep between the
5V pin hole and the GND pin hole in column 3.
